Name: Glasgow-1027
bio:
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}} == Biography == === Parentage and early life === '''Robert Glasgow''' was born probably in Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Scotland. His current estimated birth year of about 1583 is uncertain. He was the son of [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]] and [[Meik-14|Jonet Meik]]. His parentage is supported by two independent testamentary records: * Jonet Meik’s 1607 testament identifies Robert as her son. * Ninian Glasgow’s 1613 testament independently identifies Robert as his son.National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/5, testament of Jonet Meik, 1607, identifying Robert as her son; and CC9/7/9, testament of Ninian Glasgow, 1613, independently identifying Robert as his son. Transcriptions are recorded on the associated WikiTree profiles. Robert was an adult by 1613, when he was named as executor in his father’s testament. No baptismal record for Robert has yet been identified, so neither the current estimate of about 1583 nor the earlier estimate of about 1575 should be treated as exact. === Cordiner, burgess and guild brother === The 1613 Glasgow burgess roll records a '''Robert Glasgow, cordiner''', who was admitted as a burgess and guild brother as heir of a burgess.James R. Anderson, editor, ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573–1750'' (Glasgow, 1925), entry for Robert Glasgow, cordiner, in the 1613 roll. A cordiner worked in leather, commonly as a shoemaker. The timing, name and civic status make this man a strong match for Ninian Glasgow’s testament-proved son Robert. The burgess entry itself does not name the previous burgess from whom Robert inherited his entitlement, so the identification should be described as '''highly probable''' rather than independently proved by that record. His admission establishes that the matching Robert held recognised status within the Glasgow burgh community. === Marriage === Robert was associated with '''Jonet Conynghame''', whose surname also appears as '''Cunningham'''. Glasgow parish records name Robert Glasgow and Jonet Conynghame or Cunningham as parents of several children baptised between 1614 and 1627. The Scotland's People marriage index records Robert Glasgow and Jonet Conynghame at Glasgow on 6 April 1613.Scotland's People, Church of Scotland Old Parish Registers, banns and marriages, Glasgow parish 644/1, reference 230/10, Robert Glasgow and Jonet Conynghame, 6 April 1613. This was sixteen days before the 22 April 1613 burgess admission of Robert Glasgow, cordiner, and further supports—but does not by itself prove—the identification of the husband with that cordiner. === Children === Glasgow Old Parish Register entries attribute the following children to Robert Glasgow and Jonet Conynghame: * [[Glasgow-1079|Ninian Glasgow]], recorded 6 January 1614 * [[Glasgow-1080|Jonat Glasgow]], daughter, recorded 18 May 1615 * [[Glasgow-1091|Elizabethe Glasgow]], recorded 15 December 1616 * [[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]], baptised 17 November 1618 * [[Glasgow-1092|Bessie Glasgow]], recorded 24 January 1623 * [[Glasgow-1517|Elizabeth Glasgow]], recorded 24 August 1625 * [[Glasgow-1490|Catherine Glasgow]], recorded 2 October 1627 The 1618 entry records:
Robert lawful sone to Robert Glasgow & Jonet Conynghame - Godf: John & George Glasgowis.
This directly supports [[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]] as their son.National Records of Scotland, Glasgow High Kirk Old Parish Register 644/1, reported reference 10/272, baptism of Robert Glasgow, 17 November 1618; transcription: "Robert lawful sone to Robert Glasgow & Jonet Conynghame - Godf: John & George Glasgowis." The later Elizabeth may have been named after the older Elizabethe if the first child had died, but that interpretation has not been confirmed by a burial record or another contemporary source. === George and John Glasgow === John Glasgow and George Glasgow appear as witnesses or sponsors in the 1618 baptism of Robert’s son. [[Glasgow-1099|George Glasgow]] also appears in records associated with other members of the family. The repeated association suggests that he was a close relative of Robert, possibly a brother or cousin. No cited record presently states their exact relationship. George should therefore not be attached or described as Robert’s certain brother without further evidence. === Later life === No precise death date or place has been established for Robert. His documented association with Glasgow as a cordiner, burgess, guild brother and parent places him there during the early seventeenth century. Later same-name records must be assessed individually rather than assumed to concern this Robert. == Research Notes == === Birth year === Robert’s birth date is not known. Two estimates have been proposed: * about 1575, based on the assumption that he was already a mature adult when acting as executor in 1613 * about 1583, the estimate currently used on the profile The testament establishes only that Robert was old enough to act as executor in 1613. It does not supply his age or birth year. The birth date should remain uncertain. === Parentage === Robert’s parentage is directly supported by testamentary evidence. Jonet Meik’s 1607 testament calls Robert her son. Ninian Glasgow’s 1613 testament independently calls him his son. The relationships to [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]] and [[Meik-14|Jonet Meik]] may therefore be marked certain. === Identification with the 1613 cordiner === The 1613 burgess roll identifies a Robert Glasgow as a cordiner who was admitted burgess and guild brother as heir of a burgess. This is probably Ninian Glasgow’s son because: * the name and location agree * the entry occurs in the year of Ninian’s testament * Robert was already an adult and executor * admission as heir of a burgess is compatible with succession within an established Glasgow family The roll does not explicitly name Ninian as the preceding burgess. The cordiner identification is therefore highly probable, while the testamentary parentage remains the direct proof. === The November 1645 James === The original Glasgow parish register records [[Glasgow-3971|James Glasgow]] on 25 November 1645 as the son of Robert Glasgow and Jonet Cunynghame, with James Cunynghame and Johne Muir named as godfathers.Scotland's People, Church of Scotland Old Parish Registers, Glasgow parish 644/1, reference 40/56, James Glasgow, male, 25 November 1645, parents indexed as “Rot. Glasgow/Jonet Cunnyngham”. Original register image inspected 31 August 2026; it names James Cunynghame and Johne Muir as godfathers but gives no occupation, residence, age, birthplace or parentage for Robert. See also [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHK-VMK FamilySearch record VQHK-VMK], a derivative index. That entry falls about thirty-one years after the first children attributed to this couple and about twenty-seven years after their son Robert’s baptism. One couple having children across this entire period is biologically possible, but the same names in different generations, a transcription problem or a child placed one generation too high are at least as plausible. The best current reconstruction places [[Glasgow-3971|the Scottish James]] as the recorded son of a Robert Glasgow and the younger [[Cunningham-22604|Jonet Cunningham]]. [[Glasgow-1078|Robert baptised in 1618]] is a possible father, not a proved identification. Under that model, the older Robert and Jonet on this profile were James’s possible grandparents. The Scottish child must also remain separate from [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow of Kilwaughter]], whose identity with him is unproved. James should therefore remain outside this older couple’s biographical child list. The original 1645 image has now been examined: its two godfathers create a useful Cunynghame–Muir research cluster, but it supplies no detail identifying the father as either this older Robert or his son baptised in 1618. === Duplicate given names === The records presently attributed to this family include Elizabethe in 1616 and Elizabeth in 1625. Repeated use of the same name often indicates that the older child had died, but it can also result from mistranscription, duplicate indexing or two different couples. The original entries should be reviewed before drawing a firm conclusion. === Later descendants === Claims connecting Robert to [[Glasgow-1073|Rev. John Glasgow]], Alexander Glasgow or Sir Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan require documented parent-to-child evidence through every intervening generation. Surname recurrence, naming patterns and unsourced online trees are not sufficient proof of descent. === Further research === Useful next records include: * The original 1613 burgess-roll entry and related admission records * Original baptism entries for each proposed child * Records identifying the 1645 godfathers James Cunynghame and Johne Muir and their relationship, if any, to this household * Burgh court, guild, trade-incorporation and burgess records concerning Robert the cordiner * Records identifying John and George Glasgow’s relationships to Robert * Probate, property or burial records distinguishing different men named Robert Glasgow == Sources == * National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/5, testament of Jonet Meik, 1607. * National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/9, testament of Ninian Glasgow, 1613. * James R. Anderson, editor, ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573–1750'' (1925), 1613 roll. * National Records of Scotland, Glasgow High Kirk Old Parish Register 644/1, reported reference 10/272, baptism of Robert Glasgow, 17 November 1618. * Glasgow Old Parish Register entries attributed to children of Robert Glasgow and Jonet Conynghame or Cunningham.

== Biography ==
'''Jonet Cuninghame''' was born before 1597. On 6 April 1613, she married [[Glasgow-1027|Robert Glasgow]] in Glasgow, Lanarkshire.<ref name="Marriage1613">"Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTBC-P2K : 11 February 2020), Jonet Conynghame in entry for Rot. Glasgow, 1613.</ref>

Following their marriage, Jonet and Robert established their family in the city of Glasgow, where they had at least seven children baptized at the High Church between 1614 and 1627.

=== The Robertland Connection ===

Jonet's suggested parentage has not been confirmed, but a connection to the Robertland family is suggested by the marriage of her grandson, the [[Glasgow-1073|Rev. John Glasgow M.A (abt.1653-abt.1721)]],  In 1690, Rev. Glasgow married [[Cunningham-20924|Jean Cuninghame]], who is documented as the daughter of John Cunningham in Wattieston. This John Cunningham was Chamberlain to the Laird of Glengarnock and belonged to the family of Cunningham of Robertland.

=== Family ===
* '''Spouse:''' [[Glasgow-1027|Robert Glasgow (abt.1583-aft.1647)]]
* '''Marriage:''' 6 April 1613 in Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Scotland.<ref name="Marriage1613"/>

'''Children:'''
Jonet and Robert had the following children baptized in the High Church of Glasgow:
# '''Ninian Glasgow''', baptized 6 January 1614.<ref>"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch(https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHK-MJX : 16 September 2021), Jonet Conynghame in entry for Ninian Glasgow, 1614.</ref>
# '''Jonat Glasgow''', baptized 18 May 1615.<ref>"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch(https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHJ-YHJ : 16 September 2021), Jonat Conynghame in entry for Jonat Glasgow, 1615.</ref>
# '''Elizabethe Glasgow''', baptized 15 December 1616.<ref>"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch(https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHJ-5FQ : 16 September 2021), Jonet Conynghame in entry for Elizabethe Glasgow, 1616.</ref> (Likely died young).
# '''Robert Glasgow''', baptized 17 November 1618.<ref>"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch(https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHK-M42 : 16 September 2021), Jonat Conynghame in entry for Rot. Glasgow, 1618.</ref>
# '''Bessie Glasgow''', baptized 24 January 1623.<ref>"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHV-ML5 : 11 February 2020), Jonet Cuninghame in entry for Bessie Glasgow, 1623.</ref>
# '''Elizabethe Glasgow''', baptized 24 August 1625.<ref>"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch(https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHV-MLY : 16 September 2021), Jonet Cuninghame in entry for Elizabethe Glasgow, 1625.</ref>
# '''Cathren Glasgow''', baptized 2 October 1627.<ref>"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch(https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHV-96N : 16 September 2021), Jonet Cuningham in entry for Cathren Glasgow, 1627.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
* '''Conflation Warning:''' The FamilySearch source list for this family includes baptisms for children of a ''Robert Barr'' and a ''Jonat Conynghame''. This is almost certainly a different woman with the same name living in Glasgow at the same time and these children should not be attributed to this family.
* '''Reused Name:''' The baptism of two daughters named Elizabethe (1616 and 1625) strongly suggests the first child died in infancy, a common naming custom.

== Biography ==

John Glasgow was a brother of [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]] and is identified as a son of [[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow]], a fisher and burgess of Glasgow.<ref name="Ninian">James R. Anderson, ed., ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573-1750'' (Scottish Record Society, 1925), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso43scotuoft/page/24/mode/2up p. 24], entry dated 23 October 1596: “Glasgow, Ninian, B. and F., as second son to Robert G., fisher, burgess”; National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/9, images 142–145, testament testamentar and inventory of Ninian Glasgow, made 10 January 1613 and confirmed 8 May 1613: “Item to Johne glasgw his brother ane new gowne.”</ref> His date and place of birth are unknown, and his mother has not been identified.

John was living on 10 January 1613, when Ninian made his testament at Glasgow and left him a new gown.<ref name="Ninian" />

He was probably the John Glasgow who married [[Mathie-159|Jonet Mathie]], recorded as Jonat Mathen, at Glasgow on 25 January 1618.<ref name="Marriage1618">“Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910”, database, ''FamilySearch'' (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYWK-WMQ : 11 February 2020), Johne Glasgow, 1618.</ref> That couple had the following children baptised in the High Church of Glasgow:

* [[Glasgow-1088|John Glasgow]], baptised 13 May 1619.<ref name="John1619">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950”, database, ''FamilySearch'' (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHV-12T : 16 September 2021), Johne Glasgow in entry for Johne Glasgow, 1619. Mother recorded as Jonat Mathei.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-1089|Jonet Glasgow]], baptised 26 September 1622.<ref name="Jonet1622">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950”, database, ''FamilySearch'' (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHV-375 : 11 February 2020), Johne Glasgow in entry for Jonet Glasgow, 1622.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-1090|George Glasgow]], baptised 4 February 1627.<ref name="George1627">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950”, database, ''FamilySearch'' (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHK-3WB : 16 September 2021), Johne Glasgow in entry for George Glasgow, 1627.</ref>

John's date and place of death are unknown. He died after 10 January 1613, the date of the testament that securely identifies him.

== Research Notes ==

=== Parentage ===

Two records establish the family relationship. Ninian's admission as a burgess and guild brother of Glasgow on 23 October 1596 describes him as the “second son to Robert G., fisher, burgess.” His testament, made on 10 January 1613 and confirmed on 8 May 1613, names “Johne glasgw his brother.”<ref name="Ninian" />

The current assessment accepts Robert as John's father with confidence. This is a conclusion drawn from the combined records, their shared surname and compatible chronology, rather than an explicit statement of John's parentage. The testament does not distinguish between full and half-brothers, but no concrete evidence identifies a different father. The appearance of Ninian's son Robert at the 1619 baptism also supports the proposed family reconstruction, provided the identification of John with the 1618 husband is correct.

The paternal relationship and the identification of the 1618 husband are separate questions. Confidence in Robert's parentage of Ninian's brother does not establish that brother's marriage, occupation or other proposed identities.

John's mother remains unknown. Robert's documented wife Margaret Rowand is a possible mother, but no located record explicitly identifies her as such. She should not be attached as John's mother without further evidence.

=== Birth Estimate ===

No record establishes John's date or place of birth. Glasgow is a probable birthplace because of Robert's burgess status and the family's recorded connections with the burgh, but it remains unproved.

Ninian's description as Robert's “second son” does not establish John's birth order. The only direct boundary supplied by the records securely identifying John is that he was alive by 10 January 1613.

The existing “before 1572” birth estimate depends on identifying John with the adult fisher recorded in 1572–73. If that identification is correct, he was probably born no later than the early 1550s. As the identification remains unproved, it should not be used to assign a precise birth date.

=== Identification with the Husband of Jonet Mathie ===

Ninian's brother is the leading candidate for the John Glasgow who married Jonet Mathie in 1618. The strongest supporting connection is the appearance of Ninian's proved son, [[Glasgow-1027|Robert Glasgow]], among the witnesses at the baptism of John and Jonet's son John on 13 May 1619. The other witnesses were George Glasgow and Mathew Will.<ref name="John1619" /> If the child's father was Ninian's brother, Robert was witnessing the baptism of his cousin.

This is consistent with a family connection, but is not conclusive. Neither the marriage entry nor the children's baptismal entries identifies the father's occupation, property holdings or father. The records securely identifying Ninian's brother do not give his age, occupation, residence, wife or children.

The baptismal witnesses also explain an earlier, unsupported parentage proposal. George was a proved son of a different William Glasgow, while Robert was Ninian's son. Their appearance together cannot therefore establish that George, Robert and the child's father John were brothers.

The former placement of John under [[Glasgow-3522|William Glasgow]] and [[Herbison-439|Margaret Herbesoun]] relied on that interpretation of the witnesses. Those parents are not currently attached and should not be restored as proved. Witnesses may indicate a wider kinship network, but their presence alone does not define the relationships.

=== The Glasgow Fisher Recorded in 1572–73 ===

A John Glasgow appears in Robert Glasgow's property and occupational network in the early 1570s. On 12 February 1572/73, Robert and Margaret Rowand dealt with a tenement adjoining land belonging to John Glasgow, who also witnessed the transaction. On 19 December 1573, Robert and John witnessed another transaction and were described collectively as fishers.<ref name="Protocols">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 6, protocols 1903–1904, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc01renwgoog/page/n121/mode/2up 12 February 1572/73]; vol. 7, protocol 2002, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00robegoog/page/n52/mode/2up 19 December 1573].</ref>

These records establish a close property and occupational association, but do not identify John as Robert's son. More than one adult John Glasgow was active in the burgh, so the fisher remains a possible identification rather than an established one.

=== Possible Mathie Family Connections ===

The proposed marriage fits an earlier association between the Glasgow and Mathie families. On 10 May 1554, David Mathy and [[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow]] were fellow burgesses witnessing the same sasines.<ref name="Mathie1554">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 1, protocols 183–184, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07robegoog/page/n90/mode/2up 10 May 1554, printed p. 63].</ref>

David's documented son John may have been the writer later associated with the Earl of Glencairn. Tutory retours dated 20 January 1607 name Matthew, a Glasgow burgess, as the brother of the deceased John Mathie of Ibert, and list John's lawful children James, David, Agnes and Margaret.<ref name="Ibert1607">''Inquisitionum ad Capellam Domini Regis Retornatarum ... Abbreviatio'', vol. 2, tutory retours 100–101, 20 January 1607, [https://books.google.com/books?id=PiVDAAAAcAAJ digitised volume]; underlying register, National Records of Scotland, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/browsetreeview.aspx?reference=C22 C22/3].</ref>

Jonet is not named among those four children. Suggestions that she belonged to the younger Glencairn writer's household, or was an older daughter outside the tutory proceedings, remain unproved.

If John Glasgow was Robert's son, his marriage to Jonet may have renewed the association recorded between Robert Glasgow and David Mathy in 1554. That possibility does not establish Jonet's parentage or prove the identity of her husband.

=== Disputed Child: Euphame Glasgow ===

[[Glasgow-1167|Euphame Glasgow]], baptised 30 March 1634, has been proposed as another child of John Glasgow and Jonet Mathie.<ref name="Euphame1634">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950”, database, ''FamilySearch'' (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1Y9-V87 : 16 September 2021), Johnne Glasgow in entry for Euphame Glasgow, 1634.</ref>

The cited entry is an Edinburgh index record, despite Euphame's former inclusion in a list of High Church, Glasgow, baptisms. The same entry has also been used to place her in the otherwise coherent family of Rev. John Glassford and Jonet Morriel. It cannot establish both proposed fathers. Her identification remains unresolved pending examination of the original baptismal image.

=== Other John Glasgow Profiles ===

The following profiles must be distinguished before any merge is proposed:

* [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] is identified in the earlier analysis as the leading existing-profile match for Ninian's brother. Check whether this is the present profile before treating it as a separate merge candidate.
* [[Glasgow-1561|John Glasgow]] is chronologically possible, but no direct record connects him with Ninian's brother.
* [[Glasgow-3181|John Glasgow of Hirmanscheillis]] cannot be the brother named in Ninian's 1613 testament, because his estate had been processed by 4 May 1577. His death month reads March, but the year remains unresolved.

Name similarity and compatible dates are not sufficient grounds for merging these men. A further record linking John to an occupation, property, spouse, child or explicitly named father is needed to resolve the identity.

=== Saltcoats Sailor: Died December 1636 ===

A John Glasgow, sailor in Saltcoats within Ardrossan parish, died in December 1636. His testament dative came before Glasgow Commissary Court in April 1637. It names Isobell Gray as his widow and Katherine and Agnes Glasgow as the lawful children of the deceased. It does not expressly identify Isobell as their mother.<ref name="Saltcoats1637">National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, testament dative and inventory of John Glasgow, sailor in Saltcoats, NRS CC9/7/27, register pp. 478–480; original register re-read September 2026; locate by reference through the [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills Scotland's People wills search].</ref>

The sailor is chronologically compatible with this profile because John's death date is unknown. However, no examined record connects Jonet Mathie's Glasgow household with Isobell Gray, Saltcoats, the sailor occupation, Katherine or Agnes. The sailor should therefore be represented separately unless a record establishes a connection through occupation, property, residence or family.<ref name="Saltcoats1637" />

John Brown or Browne appears in the estate's financial and legal dealings, but no relationship is stated. The inventory may mention an old fishing boat and equipment; that manuscript reading remains tentative.<ref name="Saltcoats1637" />

=== Unresolved Testament Index Entry: Rashlie, 1643 ===

The printed FamilySearch index lists John Glasgow “in Rashlie, parish of Kilbride,” with a date of 17 April 1643. The full-text transcript renders the place as “Rashlic.” The entry appears in ''Glasgow. Wills 1547–1800'', item #007960708, image 112, printed index p. 196, and refers to Glasgow Commissary Court register CC9/7/28.<ref name="Rashlie1643">FamilySearch, ''Glasgow. Wills 1547–1800'', item #007960708, image 112, printed index p. 196, entry for John Glasgow in Rashlie, parish of Kilbride, 17 April 1643, Glasgow Commissary Court CC9/7/28, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS8K-D98V?view=fullText&keywords=Glasgow&searchForm=advanced&lang=en&groupId=M97N-2NT index image]. This is an image of the printed index, not the underlying testament.</ref>

This is a possible match, but the index provides no age, occupation, relative or other identifying detail connecting the Rashlie resident with this profile. Other candidates noted in the existing research are [[Glasgow-1561|John Glasgow of Linlithgow]], [[Glasgow-1084|John Glasgow]], and [[Glasgow-1088|John Glasgow, baptised in Glasgow in 1619]].

The existing notes use [[Glasgow-1084|Glasgow-1084]] for both “John Glasgow of Duddingston” and “John Glasgow of Mid Calder.” Those descriptions and links need checking before they are treated as separate candidates.

The date 17 April 1643 is the indexed testament date, not an established date of death. The underlying testament must be examined before this entry can be assigned to any of these profiles.

== Biography ==

Jonet was probably born about 1597. The date is estimated from her marriage in 1618.


Jonet married [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] in Glasgow on 25 January 1618.<ref name="Marriage1618">FamilySearch, “Scotland Marriages, 1561–1910,” John Glasgow and Jonet Mathie, 25 January 1618, Glasgow, Lanark, Scotland; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYWK-WM3 permanent record].</ref>

== Research Notes ==

=== Possible Mathie–Glasgow family connection ===

The association between the surnames can be followed for more than sixty years. On 10 May 1554 David Mathy and [[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow]] were fellow Glasgow burgesses witnessing the same sasines.<ref name="Mathie1554">Robert Renwick, ed., Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow, vol. 1, protocols 183–184, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07robegoog/page/n90/mode/2up 10 May 1554, printed p. 63].</ref> David’s son John was recorded in 1571, and may be the writer recorded in 1574 and the John Mathie admitted with the Earl of Glencairn’s burgess group in 1583.<ref name="MathieJohn">Robert Renwick, ed., Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow, vol. 6, protocol 1798, 25 October 1571, printed p. 70, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc05scogoog digitised volume]; vol. 4, protocol 1036, 4 August 1574, printed p. 19, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07scogoog digitised volume]; James R. Anderson, ed., Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573–1750, [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso43scotuoft.pdf entry for 8 February 1582/83].</ref>

In 1600 Katherine Mathy, daughter of John Mathy in Clerkland, married a Glasgow maltman; John Mathie senior and junior witnessed the transaction.<ref name="Clerkland1600">Robert Renwick, ed., Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow, vol. 11, protocol 3710, [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/abstracts_of_protocols_of_the_town_clerks_of_glasgow__1900.pdf 12 November 1600].</ref> Two successive John Mathies then served the Earl of Glencairn in 1606.

Tutory retours entered on 20 January 1607 identify the deceased John Mathie of Ibert’s full brother as Matthew Mathie, burgess of Glasgow, and name John’s lawful children James, David, Agnes and Margaret.<ref name="Ibert1607">Inquisitionum ad Capellam Domini Regis Retornatarum ... Abbreviatio, vol. 2, tutory retours 100–101, 20 January 1607, [https://books.google.com/books?id=PiVDAAAAcAAJ digitised volume]; underlying register, National Records of Scotland, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/browsetreeview.aspx?reference=C22 C22/3].</ref> The timing and Kilmaronock location make John of Ibert a strong candidate for the Glencairn servant killed in July 1606.

Jonet is not among the four children named in those tutory proceedings. She may have been older than the children requiring a tutor, but the younger Glencairn writer is presently the better candidate for her father or close kinsman. Her marriage to [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] may therefore continue the association first visible between Robert Glasgow and David Mathy in 1554.

The surname also appears as Mathei in the parish indexes. The older suggestion “Morriel” should be checked against the original marriage and baptism images.

== Biography ==

'''John Glasgow''' is recorded as born or baptised on 18 February 1616 in Mid Calder, Midlothian, with James Glasgow and Agnes Adamson attached as his parents. The older profile cited only “Old Parish Records” for this event; the original entry and the precise birth/baptism distinction remain to be checked. The supplied NRS index names James Glasgow as father (Mid Calder OPR 694/10/28), supporting a confident father relationship for this record-defined child; the later adult-identity comparisons remain provisional.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Old Parish Registers, Mid Calder, John Glasgow, 18 February 1616, father James Glasgow, parish 694, reference 10/28; supplied Scotland’s People index, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ repository].</ref>

A John Glasgow and [[Patoune-11|Helen Patoune]] were named as parents of [[Glasgow-3014|John Glasgow]], recorded on 11 January 1638 at Duddingston, Midlothian.<ref>Duddingston Old Parish Register, parish 684, reference FR38, “JOHNE GLASGOW/HELENE PATOUNE,” entry for Johne, 11 January 1638; citation carried from the former Glasgow-3015 profile. The original page has not been compared with this index wording.</ref>

Later entries name a John Glasgow with [[Porteous-912|Issobell Porteous]] as parents of [[Glasgow-1438|Issobell Glasgow]], recorded on 4 April 1643 in Edinburgh parish,<ref>“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1YN-JHD entry for Issobell Glasgow, 1643], naming John Glasgow and Issobell Porteous; cited on the child's profile.</ref> and [[Glasgow-1439|Anne Glasgow]], recorded on 20 June 1652 at Kirknewton and East Calder. The latter child's profile cites a [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/4XPK-FW2 FamilySearch tree] rather than an inspected register entry, so its details remain to be verified.

[[Glasgow-3107|James Glasgow]] is also attached as a son. His own profile documents a 1663 marriage at Polwarth but says his parentage remains unconfirmed; that attachment must not be read as an established child of this John.

== Research Notes ==

The former Glasgow-3015 profile and this profile were combined as the leading identification. The 1638 Duddingston father and the father of the 1643 and 1652 children share a name, generation and neighbouring Midlothian parishes; there is no recorded overlap in the two maternal child sequences. No death of Helen Patoune, marriage to Issobell Porteous or continuous identifier has yet been found, so identifying both fathers as one man and inferring a second union remain provisional. The earlier profile's approximate 1618 birth was an adult-status estimate, not a separate birth record.

bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]] == Biography == '''Robert Glasgow''' was born circa '''1520'''. He was a resident and citizen of Glasgow during the mid-16th century, active in civic life between at least 1551 and 1575. He appears in the civic records, particularly ''The Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', primarily as a witness and later as a property owner, identified by his occupation as a fisher. === Early Civic Appearances === On 21 May 1551 Robert witnessed the sale of a Glasgow tenement to [[Glasgow-1097|Archibald Glasgow]] and Isobell Newlands.Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 1, protocol 84, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07robegoog/page/n59/mode/2up 21 May 1551, printed p. 31]. The record places Robert with Archibald but does not state their relationship. On 10 May 1554 Robert and David Mathy were named together among the ''comburgesses'' of Glasgow while witnessing the same sasines.Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 1, protocols 183-184, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07robegoog/page/n90/mode/2up 10 May 1554, printed p. 63]. This is a direct personal association between the Glasgow and Mathie families. Protocol 266 again expressly described him as a burgess when he witnessed a property transaction on 17 February 1555/56.Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 2, protocol 266, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc08scogoog/page/n18/mode/2up 17 February 1555/56, printed pp. 2-3]. Robert continued to appear in the South Port and Clyde-bridge property district. He witnessed William Hall's sasine and immediate resale on 26 July 1557.Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 2, protocols 372-373, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc08scogoog/page/n51/mode/2up 26 July 1557, printed p. 35]. In November 1557, protocols 401 and 403 described a tenement bounded by Robert Glesgw's lands on the south and John Glesgw's lands on the west.Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 2, protocols 401 and 403, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc08scogoog/page/n57/mode/2up 8 and 26 November 1557, printed pp. 41-42]. Robert witnessed a further transaction in the same district on 20 February 1559/60, and three sasines of 18 April 1560 used his lands as a boundary; one of them also named John's lands on the west.Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 2, protocols 525-526, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc08scogoog/page/n93/mode/2up 20 February 1559/60, printed p. 76].Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 2, protocols 544-546, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc08scogoog/page/n98/mode/2up 18 April 1560, printed pp. 80-81]. These adjoining holdings establish a close property association with John, but the records state no kinship. === Marriage and Property Ownership === Robert married '''[[Rolland-239|Margaret Rowand]]''' (born c. 1535), likely around '''1551'''. By 1572, they were established citizens involved in property transactions. Protocols 1903 and 1904 call Robert and Margaret spouses when they sold property on '''12 February 1572/3'''.Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 6, protocols 1903-1904, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc01renwgoog/page/n121/mode/2up 12 February 1572/73]. The record details the transaction:
''Robert Glasgow, citizen of Glasgow, and Margaret Rowand, spouses, sold to James Rowand a tenement [...] This property, fore and back, with its pertinents, was situated on the west side of the street leading from the market cross to the South Port. It was bordered by the lands of the late Andrew Dunlop to the north, the lands of [[Glasgow-1093|John Glasgow]] to the west, the chaplainry lands of St. Roche to the south, and the street on the east. Sasine was given by Archibald Lyone, bailie, and ratified by Margaret Rowand in the absence of her husband.'' — ''12 February 1572–3, 8 a.m.''
This entry confirms Robert's marriage, his status as a property-holding citizen, and the specific location of his tenement near the market cross and South Port. It also places [[Glasgow-1093|John Glasgow]] (presumably the same fisher mentioned earlier) as the owner of the adjacent property to the west. Protocol 2125 again expressly calls Robert and Margaret Rowand spouses in a property reversion on '''7 February 1574/75'''.Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 7, protocol 2125, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00robegoog/page/n102/mode/2up 7 February 1574/75], printed p. 86. This proves Robert was alive on that date. === Family === On '''23 October 1596''', Ninian Glasgow was admitted as a burgess as the “second son to Robert G., fisher, burgess.”James R. Anderson, ed., ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573-1750'' (1925), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso43scotuoft/page/24/mode/2up p. 24], 23 October 1596. This directly proves that [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]] was Robert's second son and describes Robert as a fisher and burgess. Ninian's 1613 testament independently names “Johne glasgw his brother,” proving that Robert had another son named John who was alive on 10 January 1613.National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/9, images 142-145, testament testamentar and inventory of Ninian Glasgow, made 10 January 1613 and confirmed 8 May 1613. That John's identity remains unresolved. [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] is attached as an uncertain candidate; he must not be conflated with [[Glasgow-3181|John Glasgow of Hirmanscheillis]], who died in 1576. The records do not prove that Margaret Rowand was the mother of either son. === Death === Robert's date of death is currently unknown, but he was alive on 7 February 1574/75. The 1580 Kilbride charter is a probable later appearance; if the cross-record identification is correct, he was alive on 9 February 1580. The exact date of death remains unknown. === Burgh account, 1573-1574 === The Glasgow burgh accounts for 1573-1574 record eight shillings described as outstanding and not in use of payment from "Robert Glasgow tenement."''Extracts from the Records of the Burgh of Glasgow'', accounts for 1573-1574, printed p. 453. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QHV-V3DN-P9VH-Q FamilySearch image]. This property occurrence falls between Robert and Margaret Rowand's documented tenement transaction of February 1572/73 and their property reversion of February 1574/75. The date, city and property context strongly support attribution to this Robert, although the account itself gives no occupation, spouse or relative. == Research Notes == === Probable parentage === [[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow]] is the leading and '''probable''' father of Robert, but the relationship remains marked uncertain because no record explicitly calls Robert his son. The assessment rests on several details operating together: * William's documented son [[Glasgow-1093|John Glasgow]] and Robert repeatedly held land around the same compact South Port and Clyde-bridge property group in 1557-73. * In 1572/73 Robert and Margaret Rowand dealt with a tenement adjoining John's land, and a John Glasgow, fisher, witnessed the transaction. * Robert and John were described together as fishers in 1573.Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 7, protocol 2002, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00robegoog/page/n52/mode/2up 19 December 1573], printed p. 36. * Robert had witnessed [[Glasgow-1097|Archibald Glasgow]]'s 1551 purchase of a parcel whose exact east-of-Bargill boundary was in John's hands by 1554/55.Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 1, protocol 205, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07robegoog/page/n97/mode/2up 31 January 1554/55], printed p. 69. This is stronger than a shared surname or neighbourhood alone: it combines property, occupation and a repeated three-man association. John's service as William's sole heir is consistent with male primogeniture and does not exclude younger sons who established neighbouring holdings. The principal alternative is that the later fisher John was Robert's own son rather than William's son; both generations of John were alive during part of this period. Cousinship also remains possible. Those alternatives prevent a confident relationship status. [[Brade-232|Esbell Brade]] is William's documented wife and mother of John, but no record identifies her as Robert's mother. Her attachment therefore remains uncertain. An uncited MyHeritage tree reportedly gave Robert a birth about 1502 and named William and Esbell as parents; it is a research lead only and does not override the contemporary chronology. === Family and other claims === [[Rolland-239|Margaret Rowand]] is Robert's documented spouse, although the records do not establish a marriage about 1551 or identify her parents. Her relationship to James Rowand, who acquired the couple's property, remains worth investigating. [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]] is a documented son; the record-defined son John was alive in 1613, but his identity with [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] remains uncertain. Robert's relationship to Archibald is probably close, but the witness record does not explicitly call them brothers. Earlier descendant compilations proposed wider connections through Herbison, Stewart, Howie, Cunningham, Edmonstone, Hamilton, Ivey, Johnson, Gammon and Dauge families. Those lines require their own documentary chains and cannot establish Robert's parentage. A reported "Bigger 1625" reference has not been identified and remains unusable pending a full citation. Robert's occupation as a fisher is independently supported by protocol 2002. The exact roles of Archibald Lyone, Robert Steward, Robert Herbertsone, John Woddrop, Archibald Herbertsone, Andrew Huchesone, Duncan Lennox, John Wilsone, Hugh Blair, John Maxwell of Bogtoun, Andrew Farie and Andrew Dunlop remain associate-network questions rather than kinship evidence. === Mathie–Glencairn connection === David Mathy had a documented son John in 1571. That son may be the John Mathie who appeared as a writer in 1574 and was admitted with the Earl of Glencairn’s burgess group in 1583.Robert Renwick, ed., Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow, vol. 6, protocol 1798, 25 October 1571, printed p. 70, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc05scogoog digitised volume]; vol. 4, protocol 1036, 4 August 1574, printed p. 19, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07scogoog digitised volume]; James R. Anderson, ed., Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573–1750, [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso43scotuoft.pdf entry for 8 February 1582/83]. Tutory retours entered in 1607 identify the deceased John Mathie of Ibert’s full brother Matthew as a Glasgow burgess and name four of John’s lawful children.Inquisitionum ad Capellam Domini Regis Retornatarum ... Abbreviatio, vol. 2, tutory retours 100–101, 20 January 1607, [https://books.google.com/books?id=PiVDAAAAcAAJ digitised volume]; underlying register, National Records of Scotland, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/browsetreeview.aspx?reference=C22 C22/3]. The family therefore remained connected with both Glasgow burgh society and the Glencairn estate network. If [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] was Robert’s son, his 1618 marriage to [[Mathie-159|Jonet Mathie]] may have continued the relationship first documented between Robert and David Mathy in 1554. === Kilbride land, 1580 === On 9 February 1580 a charter of the church lands of the vicarage of Kilbride in Cunninghame, Ayrshire, named “Robertum Glasgw” among the occupiers, together with Robert Andro, Robert Boyd, Thomas Young, Robert Dunlop, Jonet Hunter, Robert Andro younger, John Wilson and John Young. The charter was confirmed under the Great Seal on 15 February 1581/82.John Maitland Thomson, ed., ''Registrum Magni Sigilli Regum Scotorum'', vol. 5, A.D. 1580–1593 (Edinburgh, 1888), no. 324, [https://archive.org/details/registrummagnisi05scot/page/104/mode/2up pp. 104–105], charter dated at Glasgow 9 February 1580 and confirmed 15 February 1581/82. The former [[Glasgow-1096]] held this Kilbride occurrence. It has been combined with this profile as the leading identity: the rare name, five-year interval after Robert and Margaret Rowand's 1575 city property act,Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 7, protocol 2125, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00robegoog/page/n102/mode/2up printed p. 86], 7 February 1574/75. and documented Mathie–Glencairn connection support one man's move or land interest in Cunninghame. Dunlop, Wilson and Young are also surnames found in the wider associated network, but shared surnames alone do not prove kinship. The charter does not call the Kilbride occupier a fisher, burgess, husband of Margaret Rowand or former Glasgow resident, so the identification remains probable rather than directly proved. The separate profile estimated birth about 1560 solely from adult occupancy in 1580; no birth record supported that year. It is compatible with the older profile's circa 1520 estimate because both are approximate adult-status inferences. If this identification is correct, Robert lived after 9 February 1580. Seek a later deed naming both his Kilbride holding and wife, occupation or Glasgow tenement to confirm the bridge. == Sources ==

bio:
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}

== Biography ==

'''Robert Glasgow''' was buried in the parish of Duddingston, Midlothian, Scotland, on '''17 January 1647'''.<ref name="RobertBurial">Church of Scotland, Old Parish Registers, Duddingston deaths and burials, burial of Robert Glasgow, 17 January 1647, parish number 684, reference 60/47, ''ScotlandsPeople''.</ref>

His date and place of birth have not been identified.

The burial entry does not state Robert's age, occupation, residence, spouse, parentage or children. It should not be assumed that every contemporary man named Robert Glasgow in Midlothian was the same person.

== Research Notes ==

=== Profile identity ===

This profile represents the '''Robert Glasgow buried at Duddingston on 17 January 1647'''.

The burial is the only record presently identified that can be assigned to this profile with reasonable certainty. Other records involving men of the same name are discussed below as possible or rejected identifications.

Because the record is a burial entry rather than an identified death entry, Robert died on or before 17 January 1647. His precise date of death is unknown.

=== Birth ===

The structured birth year of about 1582 and the Glasgow birthplace are retained as uncertain working estimates.

No inspected record states Robert's age or birthplace or supports either estimate. They should not be treated as proved facts.

Although Robert was buried in Scotland, the burial record does not establish that he was born there.

=== Possible identification at Wester Duddingston ===

On 16 June 1641 '''[[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow]]''', son of a Robert Glasgow who was servant to William Crichtoun in Wester Duddingston, was apprenticed to William Sclaitter, weaver.<ref name="JamesApprentice">Francis J. Grant, ed., [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso28scotuoft/page/71/mode/2up ''Register of Apprentices of the City of Edinburgh, 1583–1666''] (Scottish Record Society, 1906), printed p. 71: “Glasgow, James, son to Robert G., servitor to William Crichtoun, in Wester Duddingston, with William Sclaitter, weaver 16 June 1641.”</ref>

The record directly proves that:

* James's father was named Robert Glasgow;
* the elder Robert was associated with Wester Duddingston in 1641;
* Robert was then a servant to William Crichtoun; and
* James was apprenticed to William Sclaitter.

The matching surname, Duddingston locality and compatible dates make the father named in 1641 a plausible candidate for the man buried there in 1647.

The identification is not proved. Neither record supplies Robert's age, wife, occupation beyond the 1641 description, or another distinguishing relationship that securely joins the two entries.

If James remains attached as a son of this Robert, the relationship should be marked uncertain.

=== James Glasgow the Edinburgh weaver ===

The apprentice named in 1641 was later admitted as a burgess of Edinburgh on 20 June 1649. The burgess entry identifies him as a weaver, names his deceased master William Sklaitter and repeats the exact apprenticeship date of 16 June 1641.<ref name="JamesBurgess">Charles B. Boog Watson, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=218 ''Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses and Guild-Brethren, 1406–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1929), printed p. 208: “Glasgow, James, B., weiver, as p. to umq. Wm. Sklaitter, weiver, B. (16 June 1641) 20 June 1649.”</ref>

The matching master and exact apprenticeship date establish that the 1641 apprentice and the later Edinburgh burgess were the same James Glasgow.

This evidence strengthens the identification of James but does not provide additional information identifying his father with the man buried in 1647.

=== Distinct from the Inveresk James ===

The Edinburgh apprentice was not '''[[Glasgow-3923|James Glasgow]]''', who was baptised at Inveresk and Musselburgh on 19 March 1626 as a son of Alexander Glasgow and Jannet Clerk.<ref name="InvereskJames">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” database, ''FamilySearch'', [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4V-GQW James Glasgow, baptised 19 March 1626, Inveresk and Musselburgh], son of Alexander Glasgow.</ref>

The 1641 apprenticeship explicitly names Robert Glasgow, not Alexander Glasgow, as the father of the Edinburgh weaver.

The two men should remain on separate profiles.

=== Possible father ===

'''[[Glasgow-1097|Archibald Glasgow]]''' is attached as Robert's uncertain father.

Archibald and his wife Isobell Neulands are documented acquiring a tenement in Glasgow on 21 May 1551.<ref name="Archibald1551">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 1, ''First Protocol Book of William Hegait, 1547–55'' (Glasgow: Carson & Nicol, 1894), protocol 84, 21 May 1551, printed p. 31: Elizabeth Beitht sold a tenement to “Archinbald Glasgw and Isobell Neulands, spouses.” Robert Glasgw was among the witnesses.</ref>

The record does not name any children of Archibald and Isobell. It also does not state that Robert Glasgw, one of the witnesses, was Archibald's brother, son or other relative.

The proposed father-and-son relationship is chronologically possible. Archibald was married by 1551, and Robert's birth date is unknown. A son born later in the sixteenth century could have been the Robert associated with Wester Duddingston in 1641 and buried there in 1647.

There is presently no direct evidence establishing the relationship. No baptism, testament, sasine, deed or other inspected contemporary record identifies Robert as Archibald's son.

There is likewise no known record identifying a different father for Robert, and no better-supported profile has been identified as a child of Archibald.

Archibald may therefore remain attached as Robert's father with the relationship marked '''uncertain'''. The relationship should not be described as proved, probable or likely without further evidence.


=== Validator chronology note ===
WikiTree's warning that [[Glasgow-1097|Archibald Glasgow]] died before Robert was born is not a valid reading of the structured data. Archibald's death is recorded as '''after 1560''', an open lower boundary rather than a death in 1560. Robert's 1582 birth is an uncertain estimate, and their father-son relationship is itself marked uncertain. No source currently proves when Archibald died or that Robert was his son.

=== Deborah Ivey ===

'''[[Ivey-2264|Deborah Ivey]]''' has previously been attached as Robert's wife.

No Scottish marriage, baptism, testament, sasine, court record or other contemporary source has been found identifying Deborah as Robert's wife or as the mother of James Glasgow.

The attachment appears to derive from later compiled pedigrees involving Glasgow, Glasco, Glascocke or Glasscock families rather than from records concerning the Duddingston man.

Deborah should be detached from this profile.

=== Distinct from the Edinburgh cordiner ===

'''[[Glasgow-3938|Robert Glasgow]]''' married Jonet or Janet Thomsone at Edinburgh on 1 July 1652. The marriage register identifies that Robert as a cordiner.<ref name="CordinerMarriage">Henry Paton, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=278 ''Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed p. 268: “Glasgow, Robert, cordiner; Janet Thomsone 1 July 1652.”</ref>

The Duddingston Robert was buried in January 1647 and therefore could not have been the bridegroom in July 1652.

The two men are conclusively distinct and should remain on separate profiles.

No evidence presently identifies the Edinburgh cordiner as a son of the Duddingston Robert.

=== Daniel Glasco ===

Daniel Glasco, husband of Mary Gamon, is documented in Lower Norfolk County, Virginia, through the will of his father-in-law John Gamon, dated 4 October 1693 and proved 15 March 1694.

No inspected record identifies Daniel as a son of the Robert buried at Duddingston.

The supposed relationship depends on unsourced submitted pedigrees and should be removed.

There is likewise no evidence that the Duddingston Robert:

* travelled to Virginia;
* had children in colonial America;
* belonged to the Glasco, Glascocke or Glasscock families;
* married Ann Johnson or Johnston; or
* participated in any Scottish-to-Virginia migration.

=== Occupation and social status ===

If the 1641 Wester Duddingston record concerns this Robert, he was described as a servant to William Crichtoun.

The term does not establish that Robert was a merchant, burgess, property owner or participant in civic government. No evidence presently supports those descriptions.

There is also no evidence that Robert migrated from the burgh of Glasgow to Edinburgh or Duddingston. His surname alone does not identify his place of origin.

=== Wife and other children ===

No inspected record identifies the wife of the Robert buried in 1647.

James Glasgow is the only proposed child supported by a contemporary record naming a father called Robert Glasgow in Wester Duddingston. Even that identification remains uncertain because the apprenticeship record does not directly connect the father to the 1647 burial.

No other children should be attached without independent evidence.

=== Further research ===

Useful remaining research includes:

* inspection and transcription of the original 1647 Duddingston burial entry;
* Duddingston baptism, marriage and burial registers;
* neighbouring parish registers, including Canongate, Liberton and Inveresk;
* Edinburgh Commissary Court testaments;
* Midlothian sasines, rentals and property records;
* records concerning William Crichtoun of Wester Duddingston;
* household, estate or employment records naming William Crichtoun's servants;
* the original apprenticeship papers for James Glasgow;
* records of the Edinburgh Incorporation of Weavers;
* evidence identifying James Glasgow's mother;
* records naming the wife or other children of the Wester Duddingston Robert;
* a testament or estate inventory for the man buried in 1647; and
* evidence directly linking or separating the 1641 and 1647 records.

== Biography ==  
'''John Glasgow''' was born about 1590, likely in Linlithgowshire, Scotland. This estimate is based on the 1613 baptism of his daughter, [[Glasgow-3055|Jean Glasgow (bef.1613–)]]<ref>https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/sources/MG7J-6GM</ref>.

He appears in multiple parish records as the father of children baptized in the town of Linlithgow between 1613 and 1622, suggesting he resided there for at least a decade and was part of the established Glasgow family in the area.

=== Children ===  
The following children are documented in the ''Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950'' database, all born in Linlithgow, Linlithgowshire:

* '''Jean Glasgow''' – christened 17 July 1613<ref>https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1RX-HPB</ref>

=== Parentage and generation ===
[[Glasgow-3163|Andrew Glasgow]]'s operative 1598 testament expressly names four children—Marioune, James, Andrew, and William—but does not name John.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, testament of Andrew Glasgow, CC8/8/32; printed index: [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso01scotuoft/page/n117/mode/1up ''Scottish Record Society'', p. 108].</ref> John was alive and parenting children in Linlithgow from 1613 to 1622, so this omission conflicts with treating him as Andrew's proved direct son.

The existing links to Andrew and [[Anderson-103463|Jonet Anderson]] are retained as '''uncertain working parents''', not as proved relationships. The Lothian geography could instead place John one generation lower or on a collateral line through one of Andrew's documented sons, but the evidence does not identify an exact parent. Marion is Ninian's sister and is confidently identified as a daughter of
[[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow]]. Ninian's burgess admission on 23 October 1596
calls him Robert Glasgow's second son; his 1613 testament expressly calls
Marion his sister.<ref>James R. Anderson, ed., ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of
Glasgow, 1573–1750'' (Scottish Record Society, 1925),
[https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso43scotuoft/page/24/mode/2up p. 24],
23 October 1596, Ninian Glasgow, second son to Robert Glasgow, fisher,
burgess.</ref><ref name="Ninian1613" /> Together with their shared Glasgow
surname and compatible chronology, these records support the common father.
No evidence identifies a different father for Marion. The existing birth entry is a before-1592 boundary, not evidence that Marion was born in 1592. This is a confident
inference from the combined records, rather than an express father-daughter

The older profile gave James a birth year of 1670 at Kilwinning. No baptism or birth record for this adult has been found. The year and place are uncertain estimates from his adult presence there by 1689, not an independently recorded birth. His death is unknown.

Name: Glasgow-3107
bio:
== Biography == 

'''James Glasgow''' married '''Agnes Watt''' (recorded as Agnes Waitt or Waitte) on 18 June 1663 in Polwarth, Berwickshire, Scotland.<ref name="marriageRecordScotlandsPeople">“James Glasgow and Agnes Waitte,” Old Parish Registers - Banns and Marriages, National Records of Scotland (ScotlandsPeople), Parish Number 754, Ref 10/62, Frame 37, Polwarth, Berwickshire; marriage date 18 June 1663.</ref><ref name="marriageRecordFS">"Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTL8-X6D : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow, marriage to Agnes Waitte, 18 Jun 1663, Polwarth, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref> His parentage remains unconfirmed. While some online trees suggest a birth year around 1640,<ref>See, for example, the FamilySearch profile GKWN-35S which associates this marriage with a 1640 birth year, though this profile demonstrably conflates individuals (see Possible Confusions section).</ref> this is an estimate likely based on his marriage date; he was probably born in the early-to-mid 17th century.

Polwarth is a parish located in the historic county of Berwickshire, near the town of Duns. Following their marriage, James and Agnes appear to have settled in the adjacent parish of Gordon, Berwickshire. A series of baptism records in Gordon list a James Glasgow (or Glascow) as the father of several children between 1666 and 1679. Given the proximity of Gordon to Polwarth, the consistent father's name, and the timing relative to the 1663 marriage, these children are very likely the issue of James and Agnes Watt:
*   '''[[Glasgow-3117|John Glasgow (1666-)]]''', christened 29 April 1666.<ref name="johnBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTBS-Z9H : 16 September 2021), James Glascow in entry for John Glascow, christened 29 Apr 1666, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>
*   '''[[Glasgow-1440|Patrick Glasgow (abt.1667-)]]''', christened 4 August 1667.<ref name="patrickBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTBS-98Z : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Patrike Glasgow, christened 4 Aug 1667, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>
*   '''[[Glasgow-3364|Jean Glasgow (1671-)]]''', christened 16 April 1671.<ref name="jeanBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYLM-Y4Z : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Jean Glasgow, christened 16 Apr 1671, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>
*   '''[[Glasgow-3106|Robert Glasgow (1673-)]]''', christened 1 April 1673.<ref name="robertBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYHJ-3R9 : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Robert Glasgow, christened 1 Apr 1673, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>
*   '''[[Glasgow-3363|Agnes Glasgow (1676-)]]''', christened 29 October 1676.<ref name="agnesBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYLM-Y4H : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Agnes Glasgow, christened 29 Oct 1676, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>
*   '''[[Glasgow-3365|Margaret Glasgow (1679-)]]''', christened 24 May 1679.<ref name="margratBaptismFS">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYL9-Q32 : 16 September 2021), James Glasgow in entry for Margrat Glasgow, christened 24 May 1679, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>

The christening of a daughter named Agnes in 1676 strongly supports the identification of this family unit with the 1663 marriage of James Glasgow and Agnes Watt, following common naming patterns. While the indexed baptism records from FamilySearch do not include the mother's name, the circumstantial evidence linking these Gordon children to James and Agnes (Watt) of Polwarth is compelling.

Further evidence of the family's presence in Gordon comes from the marriage record of their daughter, Jean. On 3 June 1702, '''John Smith''' married '''Jean Glasgow''' in Gordon, Berwickshire. The record explicitly names the bride's father as '''James Glasgow'''.<ref name="jeanMarriageFS">"Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTLH-1MB : 11 February 2020), James Glasgow in entry for John Smith and Jean Glasgow, 3 Jun 1702, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref> This confirms Jean survived to adulthood and indicates the family's continued connection to the Gordon parish into the early 18th century. The record identifies James as Jean's father but does not necessarily confirm he was still living in 1702.

Beyond these records, specific details about James's occupation or death date remain unconfirmed in contemporary Scottish sources.

== Research Notes ==

Likely a relative of the father of a William Glasgow, father of [[Glasgow-1605|William Glasgow (bef.1658-)]] in Polworth, Berwickshire. These are the first two Glasgow's to appear in this area. (brothers?) 

=== Possible Confusions with Ulster Glasgows ===
Genealogical research on this James Glasgow is complicated by the presence of other men with the same name in 17th-century records, particularly in Ulster, Ireland. Several online genealogies and collaborative trees (such as FamilySearch profile GKWN-35S, which attaches the Polwarth marriage, the Gordon baptisms, ''and'' a 1725 death date) have mistakenly connected James Glasgow of Polwarth and Gordon to the James Glasgow who settled in Kilwaughter Parish, County Antrim, Ireland. This Kilwaughter James appears in the 1669 Hearth Money Rolls for County Antrim and reportedly died in 1726.<ref name="kilwaughterInfo">This information regarding the Kilwaughter James is commonly cited in Glasgow family histories but requires primary source verification for the death date and details. Secondary sources often cite a James Glasgow in Kilwaughter, Co. Antrim, appearing in the 1669 Hearth Money Rolls and dying c. 1726. Primary source verification is recommended. This individual is considered distinct from James Glasgow of Polwarth/Gordon.</ref>

Crucially, there is currently no known documentary evidence directly linking the James Glasgow who married Agnes Watt in Polwarth (1663) and raised a family in Gordon, Berwickshire (c. 1666-1679+), to the James Glasgow recorded in Kilwaughter, County Antrim. The established family life in Berwickshire during the period the Kilwaughter James was documented in Ireland strongly suggests these were two distinct individuals. Researchers should treat them separately. The 1725/1726 death date often associated with James Glasgow belongs to the Kilwaughter individual, not the James of Polwarth and Gordon.

== Biography ==

'''John Glasgow''' is estimated to have been born about 1813 in Ireland. An unsourced family tree handed down to [[Glasgow-933|M Glasgow]] identifies him as the husband of Elizabeth Fee and places their marriage before 1845 in Ireland.<ref name="FamilyTree">Unsourced family tree handed down to [[Glasgow-933|M Glasgow]].</ref> Those details remain a family reconstruction rather than a proved identification.

== Research Notes ==

=== Parentage and identity ===

The 1851 census of [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow]]'s Glenleslie household records his son John, aged forty, a labourer, absent in '''America'''.<ref name="Glenleslie1851">[https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf ''1851 Irish Census Returns: detailed comma-delimited transcription''], Glenleslie household 23.</ref> That census-identified man now has the separate profile [[Glasgow-4055|John Glasgow]]. This profile is retained for the County Armagh family attached through Elizabeth Fee and Samuel; no record links that family to Robert's absent son.

Robert's son was not the same person as the forty-year-old nephew living with [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]] in nearby household 21. The nephew was resident at Glenleslie, worked as a linen weaver and reported a first marriage in 1839.<ref name="Glenleslie1851" />

=== County Armagh family ===

The family attached through Elizabeth Fee and their reported son Samuel points instead toward County Armagh. A published biography of Samuel's son states that Samuel came from Armagh to Queensland in 1863.<ref name="SenateBio">[https://biography.senate.gov.au/glasgow-thomas-william/ Biographical Dictionary of the Australian Senate], Thomas William Glasgow.</ref>

A separate John Glasgow, widowed farmer, died at Killyreavy, County Armagh, on 27 December 1882 aged 66. His son-in-law James Campbell reported the death.<ref name="KillyreavyDeath">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1883/06378/4830400.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register], John Glasgow, Killyreavy, 27 December 1882.</ref> Campbell had married Martha Jane Glasgow, daughter of John Glasgow, farmer of Killyreavy, on 20 February 1873.<ref name="CampbellMarriage">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1873/11258/8128996.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], James Campbell and Martha Jane Glasgow, First Keady Presbyterian Church, 20 February 1873.</ref> These records establish a distinct Armagh John and daughter, but do not yet prove that he was Elizabeth Fee's husband or Samuel's father.

The exact identity of the County Armagh John remains unresolved. He should not be merged with [[Glasgow-4055|Robert's census-identified son]] unless a record explicitly connects the two families.

* Candidate death entry: John Glasgow, 11 December 1882, aged 66, Armagh district, D/1883/11/1002/12/140. [https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/death GRONI death index].

bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]] {{Estimated Date|Birth}} == Biography == '''Andrew Glasgow''' (written ''Andro Glasgw'') lived at a place read uncertainly as “Corsoun,” in the parish read as “Calder Clair” or “Calder Cleir,” within the sheriffdom of Edinburgh. His testament testamentar and inventory was made on 6 February 1597 as written (1597/8). The record says that he died the next day, 7 February, and was confirmed on 10 July 1598.National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/32, images 123–124, testament testamentar and inventory of Andro Glasgw, made 6 February 1597/8, death stated as 7 February, confirmed 10 July 1598; working transcription of the original register images. See also Scottish Record Society, ''Commissariot of Edinburgh: Register of Testaments, 1514–1600'', [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso01scotuoft/page/n117/mode/1up p. 108]. This was a ''testament testamentar'': Andrew made the will himself on the day before his death. The introductory account, inventory and debts begin on image 123; the family provisions continue on image 124. A different testament begins towards the foot of image 124 and is not part of Andrew's entry. === Family and executors === Andrew's wife was '''Elizat Stevinsoun''' (Elizabeth Stevenson). The testament expressly calls '''Robert Glasgow''' their son:
“Robart Glasgw his sone begottin be him vpoun the said Elizat his wyff”
It also names Andrew's daughters '''Marion, Janet and Isobel'''. The dispositive clause refers to “his said sone and his said [dochter… struck through] Marione, Jonet, Isobell.” {| class="wikitable sortable" style="padding: 5px; width:100%;" |+ '''Household named in Andrew Glasgow's testament''' |- ! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Person ! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Relationship ! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | What the record proves |- | Elizat Stevinsoun || Wife || Appointed with Robert to administer the movable estate; explicitly called Andrew's spouse and wife. |- | Robert Glasgow || Son || Explicitly Andrew's son by Elizat; he had not yet reached the age fixed for taking the land. |- | Marion Glasgow || Daughter || Named in the operative inheritance clause as one of Andrew's daughters. |- | Janet Glasgow || Daughter || Named in the same inheritance clause. |- | Isobel Glasgow || Daughter || Named in the same inheritance clause. |- | Unnamed possible child || Conditional only || Provided for only if Elizat was pregnant; the will does not prove a later birth. |} Andrew appointed Elizat and Robert to take charge of his goods, movable property and debts receivable, and to pay his debts. He also named advisers whose counsel they were to use. One readable adviser was '''James Stevisoun'''. The shared surname makes him a useful lead for Elizat's family, but the will does not call him her father, brother or other relative. === Estate and financial network === The inventory describes a working rural household. It appears to include three cows with calves, although the number is uncertain; two yearling cattle; two horses valued at £10 each, £20 altogether; nine sheep; eight bolls of oats in the barn and barnyard; four firlots of barley; household utensils and furnishings; and Andrew's clothing. Several quantities, individual valuations and the inventory total remain unresolved and should not be supplied from the usual form of other testaments. The debts owed to Andrew include entries for '''John Mure''', an incompletely identified widow of a deceased John, and '''James Stevisoun'''; some residences and all of the relevant sums remain uncertain. The debts Andrew owed include a payment associated with a brown horse, and less secure readings involving Bartholomew Wilson, James Lyon and John Brown, David Lyon, James Stevisoun and a laird whose designation may be Westhall. These are economic associates, not proved relatives. The account then calculated the free estate, its division into thirds and Andrew's own third, but the figures have not been securely read. === Distribution and land === Andrew directed that, once his debts had been paid, one third of the free estate should go to Elizat and another third to Robert. His own third was to go to a child if Elizat was pregnant by him. If she was not pregnant, that third was to be divided equally among Robert, Marion, Janet and Isobel. Andrew provided that Elizat was to “bruik his [word unclear] land quhill his said Robart cum to aige”: she was to possess or enjoy the land until Robert reached legal age. The unclear word before ''land'' is not supplied here. This is direct evidence of intended succession within Andrew's household, but the record does not say from whom Andrew obtained the land or whether his interest was heritable or tenanted. The will also allowed for the possibility that Elizat was pregnant: “incais his said spous be with bairne to him.” That conditional wording does not establish that another child was born. Andrew further directed that, if “Elizat his spous do not hir pairt to his said bairnis,” she was to be removed from the administration, protecting the children's interests. The closing clause records execution by a notary at Andrew's direction because he could not write. The subsequent confirmation again names Elizat Stevinsoun and Robert Glasgow. A further man, Johne Sandelandis, appears in the confirmation, but the surviving reading does not establish a relationship to the family. == Research Notes == === Calendar and locality === The manuscript year is 1597 in the Scottish record, while the confirmation was in July 1598. Andrew's death should therefore be recorded as 7 February 1597/8, not 10 July 1598. The readings “Corsoun” and “Calder Clair/Cleir” remain qualified until the handwriting is independently resolved. The place has been rendered both Corsoun and Corstoun in derivative work. It has not been safely equated with a modern settlement. The profile's structured death place should reflect only the documented household locality, marked uncertain, rather than the unsupported Kirknewton value. === Corrected family reading === An earlier transcription identified a Jonet Anderson as Andrew's wife and Marion, James, Andrew and William as four children. Re-reading images 123–124 does not support that reconstruction. The secure relationships are Elizat Stevinsoun as wife; Robert as Andrew and Elizat's son; and Marion, Janet and Isobel as Andrew's daughters. Profiles [[Glasgow-4006]] and [[Glasgow-4007]] represent supposed sons Andrew and William from that reading; neither man is named as Andrew's child in the corrected testament. Their profiles should preserve the history of the mistake without treating it as evidence that either person existed. The current spouse should not be detached merely to leave an empty field before an evidenced Elizabeth profile is available, but the relationship is contradicted and must not be presented as proved. Robert, Marion, Janet and Isobel each require a new documentary profile. [[Glasgow-1156]], [[Glasgow-3062]], [[Glasgow-3917]], [[Glasgow-3183]] and [[Glasgow-3336]] were compared but do not have a direct Corsoun, Stevenson, sibling, property or succession bridge. They must not be substituted merely from name, chronology or regional compatibility. The currently attached [[Glasgow-991|James Glasgow]], [[Glasgow-1561|John Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1028|David Glasgow]] are not named as sons in this testament. They should remain uncertain unless another record independently connects them to Andrew. The attached spouse is now the record-defined Elizat Stevinsoun (Elizabeth Stevenson). The earlier Jonet Anderson identification is retired. The earlier model reading of the 1577 testament's second child as ''Androw'' has been superseded by the accepted Marjory (''m[ar]iory'') reading, so no comparison with this Andrew profile arises from that record. The 1577 household is associated with the place provisionally indexed as Hirmenschelis, while this testament places Andrew at Corsoun; no record bridges the two households, and this profile is not the present match for any child of [[Glasgow-3181|John Glasgow]]. === Parentage and next evidence === No parent is named. [[Glasgow-1093|John Glasgow]] remains an uncertain working father only; Andrew's evidence is in the rural Calder setting, whereas John's proved family is concentrated in Glasgow burgh records. The highest-value next search is the National Records of Scotland's Morton estate material: GD150/696–757 (Barony of Caldercleir), GD150/2027–2060 (Midlothian rentals), and GD150/320–493. An occupier succession naming Robert after Andrew could identify The proved son and clarify the nature of the landholding.National Records of Scotland, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=GD150 GD150, Papers of the Earls of Morton], especially GD150/696–757, GD150/2027–2060 and GD150/320–493. == Sources ==
